info.name: AOD Backend
info.description: Auth, profile, team, and session endpoints for the AOD backend. Import the accompanying environment file too — run Login or Register once and the `token` variable fills itself in for every other request. Team endpoints act on the caller's own active team automatically; the `team_id` variable is only needed if you want to override that via `?team=`. The Sessions folder walks the full lifecycle: create -> join -> consent -> start -> complete. Completing a session moves it to `processing` and queues an AssemblyAI transcription per stored AOD.

request.description: role: Coach | Player. Coach may send team_action=create with team_name (and optional description) to create a team, or team_code to request joining one, or neither to register teamless. Player may send team_code to request joining, or omit it to register teamless. riot_id is required for Player and prohibited for Coach.

query.description: Optional. Omit to use your own active team automatically.

request.description: Returns the team plus its active members (data.team.members) and the team_code, both shown to any active member regardless of role. Resolves to your own active team automatically — the ?team= query param is disabled by default; enable it only to look up a different team.
Main coach only. Acts on your own active team; append ?team={id} to target a different one.

query.description: Optional. Omit to use your own active team automatically.

request.description: Detection settings for the team: dead_air_threshold_ms plus the informative_keywords and declarative_keywords lists. Any active Coach (main or assistant); non-coach members get 403, non-members 404.

query.description: Optional. Omit to use your own active team automatically.

request.description: Replaces the detection keyword list. Send the COMPLETE desired list per category (same shape as GET /teams/settings) — both keys required; the server inserts new words and deletes any word you omit. Single words only (no spaces), 1-64 chars, max 200 per category; matching is case-insensitive and a word may not appear in both categories. The list is also what gets sent to AssemblyAI as a word-boost list when a session's AODs are transcribed. Any active Coach; non-coach 403, non-member 404. Returns the full settings body.

item.name: Sessions
item.description: One recorded game, from lobby (`queuing`) through `in_progress` to `processing`. Lifecycle: Create -> players Join -> players Consent -> Coach Start -> Coach Complete. Completing carries an audio + video slot per recording player, stores the AOD/VOD records, moves the session to `processing`, and queues one AssemblyAI transcription per stored AOD. `processing` is not a terminal state and does not block the team from starting the next session.

query.description: asc | desc by created_at, default desc.

request.description: Any active team member. Returns `data.live_session` (the team's single `queuing` or `in_progress` session, or null) plus a paginated `data.past_sessions` list of everything else. A `processing` session is not "live": it appears in `past_sessions`, and its entry carries a `transcription` progress block, e.g. `"transcription": { "total": 5, "completed": 3, "failed": 0 }`. Non-processing entries omit that key.

Any active Coach (main or assistant). Creates a `queuing` session and joins the creating Coach as its first participant. Rejected with 422 if the team already has a `queuing` or `in_progress` session (a `processing` one does not block a new one). The Timeline row is NOT created here — it is created when the session is completed and enters `processing`. Captures `session_id` from the response.

Any active member of the session's team. Returns the session and its active participants. Refused with 409 ("This session is still processing.") while the session is `processing` — read progress from List Team Sessions instead.

Any active team member, while the session is `queuing`. Idempotent: joining again is a no-op success. A member who previously left is reactivated. Snapshots the caller's current team role onto the participant row.

The caller's own participant row moves needs_consent -> ready. Idempotent once ready. A Coach has nothing to consent to (422). Consent closes once the session is no longer `queuing`/`in_progress` (422).

Any active Coach on the session's team. Moves `queuing` -> `in_progress` and every consented player to `recording`. Rejected with 422 unless the session is `queuing`, at least one player has joined, and every joined player has consented.

Any active Coach on the session's team. Moves a `queuing` or `in_progress` session to `cancelled`. No AOD/VOD is ever persisted before `processing`, so cancelling mid-run discards nothing that was saved. A `processing` or already-terminal session is rejected with 422.

formdata.description: Must equal the recording roster exactly across all slots: one slot per player currently in `recording`, no extras, none missing.
Optional. mp3/wav/aac/ogg/webm/m4a, max 200 MB. The AOD: this is what gets sent to AssemblyAI.
Optional. mp4/webm/mov/mkv, max 2 GB. The VOD: stored only, not transcribed.

request.description: Any active Coach on the session's team. multipart/form-data, one `players[N][user_id]` slot per recording player plus optional `players[N][audio]` / `players[N][video]` files. Single-shot: the session completes once at least one slot holds BOTH an audio and a video. On success it stores the AOD/VOD records, creates the Timeline, moves `in_progress` -> `processing`, sweeps every recording participant to `completed`, and (after the transaction commits) queues one AssemblyAI transcription job per stored AOD. Response `data.session.status` is `processing`. Rejected with 422 if the session is not `in_progress`, the submitted user ids do not match the recording roster exactly, or no slot holds a full pair. Enable the `players[1][...]` rows for a second player.
